filename: Simulating Atmospheric Processes in Earth System Models and Quantifying Uncertainties with Deep Learning Multi-Member and Stochastic Parameterizations.pdf
title: Simulating Atmospheric Processes in Earth System Models and Quantifying Uncertainties with Deep Learning Multi-Member and Stochastic Parameterizations
venue: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
parameterization_target: Subgrid convective and turbulent processes, cloud condensate tendencies, and surface radiative fluxes from a cloud superparameterization
testbed_rationale: Provides open benchmark data sample on Zenodo, fully archived training/test runs, and open source code for offline and online coupled training of stochastic/multi-member neural network parameterizations in CESM2.
pain_points: Fully coupled ML models suffered immediate stratospheric ice growth instability and radiation blowups within days.

Learning cloud condensate tendencies (liquid and ice water) is very inaccurate offline (R2 < 0.3) and destabilizes the climate model, necessitating a costly partial-coupling workaround where SP runs concurrently to handle condensates.
Partial coupling drastically increases computational expense, running slower than the original SP-CESM.
Monte Carlo Dropout severely underestimated spread and was strongly underdispersive.
Hybrid simulations developed severe thermodynamic biases (over 20 K stratospheric and Antarctic temperature bias, equatorial dry bias), causing ITCZ shift and weakening.
Sensitivity to simulation initialization dates causing initialization shocks.
extraction_notes: The paper investigates three stochastic/ensemble deep learning methods (MC Dropout, Multi-Member DNNs, and Latent Space Perturbation in VEDs) to emulate a superparameterization in CESM2. Online simulation survived 5 months only using 'perfect condensate' partial coupling.
